clipA: Beautiful hand-painted 2D animation style, reverent and warm, like a classic illustrated storybook of scripture brought to life. Soft painterly brushstroke textures, glowing golden light, muted earth tones with warm gold highlights. First-century Judea. Sacred, hushed tone. Not photorealistic. No text or captions in the image. Historically modest clothing: rough-woven wool and linen in undyed earth colors. No modern objects. Slow, tender movement. The camera holds low inside the dim packed room looking up at the ragged hole in the clay ceiling where a blazing shaft of daylight pours through drifting dust and falling straw. Through the whole clip the woven reed mat carrying the thin paralyzed man descends slowly and steadily down the column of light on its four corner ropes - visibly LOWER in the frame with every passing second, starting just below the ceiling and ending as it settles gently onto the earthen floor - the four taut ropes paying out hand over hand from the four men gripping them above, the mat swaying gently and leveling as it comes down. The crowd below eases backward to make room, upturned faces following the mat down. The man on the mat lies still, arms resting, legs under the faded ochre blanket, exactly two arms and two legs. No figure changes position except as described.
clipB: Beautiful hand-painted 2D animation style, reverent and warm, like a classic illustrated storybook of scripture brought to life. Soft painterly brushstroke textures, glowing golden light, muted earth tones with warm gold highlights. First-century Judea. Sacred, hushed tone. Not photorealistic. No text or captions in the image. Historically modest clothing: rough-woven wool and linen in undyed earth colors. No modern objects. Slow, tender movement. In the column of dusty daylight the thin man with short dark curly hair rises from the reed mat through the whole clip in one continuous believable motion: he pushes up from the floor, gets one foot flat, straightens on trembling legs, finds his balance with arms slightly spread, then bends and lifts the rolled reed mat under one arm and takes his first careful steps forward as the awestruck crowd pulls back to open a path. His legs move in a real walking cycle, each foot lifting and planting in turn. His face moves from concentration to disbelieving joy. Exactly two arms and two legs on every figure at every moment; nobody else crosses the frame.
